title: Proper and open factors in datum coordinates
statement: Let \(D\) be a finite-field datum, \(B(X)\) a category for every six-functor space \(X\) over \(D\), \(S\) a six-functor push stage on \(B\), and \(T_X:B(X)\to[B(X),B(X)]\) the curried tensor functors. Let \(Q\) be a compactified square and \(A\) exchange data for \((S,T,Q)\), as in [def-sf-operation-stages]. For \(K\in B(Q.X)\) and \(L\in B(Q.Y)\), define \(\mathrm{first}(A,K,L)\) as the source equality transport, tensor of the specified compact-support identification, and the proper adjunction projection mate. Define \(\mathrm{second}(A,K,L)\) as proper image of the open projection, the inverse compact-support identification, and the target equality transport. Their intermediate object is \(A.\mathrm{properPush}(T_{\bar X}(A.\mathrm{openExtension}(K),A.\mathrm{properPull}(L)))\). The projection component of \(A\) equals first followed by second. All transports and operations are the specified data, with no new choice. Two commutative coefficient squares paste along such a factorization: given a functor F between any categories and composable arrows a,b,c,s,p,q,m,t with the indicated endpoints, if s followed by p is F(a) followed by m, m followed by q is F(b) followed by t, and a followed by b is c, then s followed by p followed by q is F(c) followed by t. This last assertion uses only associativity and functoriality in arbitrary categories.
